stories.title: UP weather machines show faulty flood alerts:₹137 crore paid to company despite official warnings on system faults
stories.summary: In UP, when there is light rain, the meteorological department's machines are showing flood-like conditions. If clouds appear, they are sending messages of sunshine. This malfunction is due to the Automatic Weather Stations and Automatic Rain Gauges installed 2 years ago. A Hyderabad company had installed these machines in all tehsils and blocks. After receiving initial data from these machines, the Meteorological Department wrote a letter to the Relief Commissioner- The equipment is not providing accurate data. Temperatures below 44C are being shown as over 50C. Light rain is being reported as heavy rain. Please consider before making payment. Despite this, the Relief Department paid Rs 137 crore to the Hyderabad contractor company. The result is that the Meteorological Department is unable to get accurate information about storms and rain. Know where the matter started from Stations were built for weather forecasting, machines were installed In 2023, the Relief Department decided to install Automatic Weather Stations and Automatic Rain Gauges in 826 blocks and 351 tehsils of UP for accurate weather forecasting. The project was approved in the State Executive Committee meeting. A fund of 141.6 crore rupees was received to install 450 weather stations and 2000 automatic rain gauges in UP. After the tender process, the department awarded the contract to Hyderabad-based company Obel Systems Private Limited for 137 crores to install both machines. The company installed the equipment at tehsils and blocks in UP. The Meteorological Department did the verification The contract stipulated that the verification of the operation of these devices would be done by the Meteorological Department. Verification had to be done on 3 points- After verification, the Meteorological Department had to submit a report. Only after finding everything correct in this, the Relief Department had to make payment to the company installing the machines. Discrepancies found in verification On June 21, 2025, Director of Meteorological Department Dr. Manish R. Ranalkar wrote a letter to the then Relief Commissioner Bhanuchandra Goswami. He informed that the machines are not giving correct data (readings). The data received from weather stations is saved on IMD's Pune server. This data is also stored on the UP government's web portal. Due to incorrect data, IMD (Lucknow) is unable to make accurate weather predictions. The director further wrote - When we verify and compare this data, discrepancies are coming to light. When will the heat increase? When will the weather remain normal? Will it rain or not? Difficulties are arising even in estimating such basic information. Suggestion given - The quality of these machines' network should be checked. Also, attention needs to be paid to maintenance. Temperature and rainfall predictions proved wrong 1. Reality 44C, machine showing over 50C The machines installed at the weather station are giving incorrect feeds regarding temperature. When the temperature at the meteorological department's own centers doesn't even reach 44C, these new machines were recording temperatures above 50C. That is, there wasn't as much heat on the ground as these machines were showing. 2. When not a drop fell from the sky, machines recorded 'heavy rainfall' The condition of the station machines is such that even in scorching heat, they were giving data of 'torrential rain'. The limit was crossed when these machines recorded several times more rainfall compared to the actual IMD (India Meteorological Department) centers. That is, where light drizzles occurred, these machines gave data indicating 'flood'-like conditions. This was making it difficult for the department to provide accurate weather forecasts. According to the Director of the Meteorological Department, behind this major system failure were these negligences by the department and the company- Company's Major Negligence: Neither Conducted Inspection, Nor Corrected Data The Director of the Meteorological Department raised questions about the work of the Hyderabad-based company 'Obel Systems' in his letter. The department had asked the company to implement a data verification system on the server, so that bad or incorrect data could be filtered out and accurate information could be obtained. However, the company did not create any such system. The department had given strict instructions that the company should get its sensors re-examined by IMD Pune or any government-recognized (NABL) lab. The company did not get the sensors examined even once. The company was supposed to carry out maintenance of stations and inspection of machines from time to time. The report says that the company neither did maintenance nor tested the machines. The director wrote that Obell System Pvt. Ltd. did not comply with the tender conditions. Payment to the firm should be considered only after verification. Delhi lawyer's claim - Meeting with company at Jhansi hotel Delhi advocate Abhishek Saxena filed a complaint with the CBI. He alleged that the then Relief Commissioner Bhanuchandra Goswami and his OSD Manoj Kumar met with MD of Obell System Pvt. Ltd., O. Reddy, at a hotel in Jhansi on October 3, 2024. The deal was finalized in this meeting. What is Obell Systems Private Limited? Obell Systems Private Limited company was started in 1999 with the name Obell Computers Private Limited. In 2012, the company's name was changed to Obell Projects Private Limited. In 2016, the company's name was changed to Obell Systems Private Limited. The company has so far installed 2978 Automatic Weather Stations, 6429 Automatic Rain Gauges, and 137 Automatic Water Level Recorders in different states. Now the officials' statement We reported the defects in the machines In this entire matter, Director of Meteorology Department Dr. Manish R. Ranalkar says, 'We had submitted our report to the Relief Commissioner's office. In this, the defects that were there in the Automatic Weather Stations and Automatic Rain Gauges were mentioned. We had stated that payment should be made only after verification as per tender conditions. After that, no report was taken from us.'

stories.title: ‘If religion is attacked, Yogi will not remain silent’:UP CM recalls grand Ram Temple construction in Ayodhya
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said that anyone attempting to attack religion would receive a “strong response,” asserting that his government would not remain silent in such situations. Addressing a gathering on Monday, at the idol installation ceremony at Shri Shiv Gorakhnath Ashram in Bhagwanpur Nangal village of Baghpat district, the Chief Minister referred to the construction of the Ram Temple in Ayodhya and said, “A grand Ram Temple was built in Ayodhya. Could anyone stop it? No one could.” He also took an apparent swipe at political opponents, saying some people secretly took COVID-19 vaccines and visited the Sangam for a holy dip but publicly denied doing so. Participated in religious ceremony at Gorakhnath Ashram The Chief Minister reached the Shri Shiv Gorakhnath Ashram on Monday, where he offered prayers and attended the idol consecration programme. During his address, Yogi Adityanath said the day was significant because it marked the anniversary of the re-consecration of the Somnath Temple. “Today, the Prime Minister himself was present at the Somnath Swabhiman celebration at the temple. I also had the privilege of being associated with this occasion at the Kashi Vishwanath Temple,” he said. Recalled Pokhran nuclear tests The Chief Minister also referred to India’s nuclear tests conducted on May 11, 1998, under former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee. “On this very day, Atalji conducted three nuclear tests in Pokhran under Operation Shakti. After that, India emerged as an important nuclear power, and the world was left astonished by India’s success,” he said. Yogi Adityanath added that Sanatan Dharma had never tried to forcibly rule or enslave others. “History is witness that Sanatan Dharma never forcibly occupied anyone’s land or enslaved people. That is why our country cannot tolerate aggression against itself,” he said. ‘Baghpat is a sacred land linked to Mahabharata’ The Chief Minister described Baghpat as a historically and spiritually significant place linked to the Mahabharata. He said Baghpat was among the five villages that Lord Krishna had sought from the Kauravas for the Pandavas. “Today Baghpat has become a district. When I visited here four years ago, it was a small place. I thank those who transformed it into a pilgrimage centre,” he said. He also praised Rashtriya Lok Dal leader Jayant Chaudhary and former Mumbai Police Commissioner Satyapal Singh, saying development and heritage were progressing together in the region. ‘Religion protects those who protect it’ Quoting the Sanskrit phrase “Dharmo Rakshati Rakshitah,” Yogi Adityanath said people must protect religion, as religion in turn protects society. “We should never knowingly or unknowingly harm the nation or religion. Damage to religion cannot be compensated,” he said. Claims improvement in jobs and law order The Chief Minister said recruitment opportunities had increased significantly in Baghpat and surrounding districts in recent years. “Earlier, recruitments did not take place here. Today, thousands of youths are getting jobs without discrimination, including youths from Baghpat, Muzaffarnagar, and Saharanpur,” he said. He also claimed that women and traders now feel safer in Uttar Pradesh and that investments were increasing in the state. Gorakhnath Ashram has 400-year-old legacy According to local accounts, the Shri Shiv Gorakhnath Ashram has a history of nearly 400 years. It is believed that saints Baba Chhotenath and Baba Lichhinath attained samadhi at the site after years of penance. Spread across nearly 23 bighas of land, the ashram houses several temples dedicated to Lord Shiva, Hanuman, Bhairav, Shani Dev, Navnath saints, and Guru Gorakhnath. The samadhi sites of Baba Chhotenath and Baba Lichhinath are considered spiritually significant by devotees. The ashram continues to serve as a centre for yoga, meditation, devotional singing, and Nath sect traditions. In 2022, the Uttar Pradesh Tourism Department carried out beautification work at the ashram worth Rs 6.16 crore. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath had also visited the site in 2023.

stories.title: Bulldozer action on 125-year-old 'Musafirkhana' in Kashi:25 houses demolished in Daalmandi road-widening project
stories.summary: A 125-year-old 'Musafirkhana' building in Varanasi’s Daalmandi area was partially demolished on Monday as part of an ongoing road-widening project. Workers demolished the boundary wall built over the structure, while heavy police deployment remained in place to maintain law and order. Around 300 police personnel, along with paramilitary forces, were deployed in the area during the operation. Authorities also monitored the entire locality through drone surveillance. ‘Musafirkhana’ among 45 buildings marked for demolition The demolition is part of the Daalmandi Road Project, under which the existing road is being widened. A total of 45 buildings, including the Musafirkhana, fall within the project zone. The 'Musafirkhana', managed by the Waqf Board, was traditionally used as a lodging facility for travellers and also hosted wedding functions. Officials said that within the last three days, 25 houses have already been demolished using three JCB machines and around 50 labourers. The Waqf Board had been given 12 days to vacate and prepare for demolition. See 3 pictures Daalmandi has historical link to Sanjay Dutt’s family The Daalmandi area also has a connection to Bollywood actor Sanjay Dutt’s family. His grandmother, Jaddanbai, is believed to have lived in the locality. Heavy security deployment during demolition A joint team of Public Works Department (PWD) and Municipal Corporation officials reached the site on Monday morning along with police and paramilitary personnel. The area was barricaded from all sides to prevent any untoward incident during the demolition drive. PWD officials said the target is to demolish all 45 identified structures, including 20 buildings that had already been declared unsafe by the Municipal Corporation. Officials had earlier carried out demolition of 20 houses on May 9 and five more houses on May 10. ACP says, ‘Action will continue’ Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) Atul Anjan Tripathi said action was being taken against dilapidated buildings and properties registered under the PWD acquisition process. “The operation will continue continuously. Adequate security force has been deployed because the Nai Sadak and Chowk areas are highly crowded zones,” he said. 'Musafirkhana' was more than a century old PWD Executive Engineer K.K. Singh said the Musafirkhana building was approximately 125 years old and had undergone repairs and modifications over time. “At present, the building was being managed by the Waqf Board and was used for lodging and wedding-related events,” Singh said. He added that a meeting had earlier been held between the district administration and the Waqf Board, during which the board requested 12 days’ time before the demolition. After the deadline ended, the demolition was carried out without resistance. 60 houses already demolished earlier For the Daalmandi road-widening project, authorities have identified a total of 187 properties, including 181 houses and six mosques. PWD first began demolition work in the area on October 29, 2025. So far, 60 houses have already been demolished, while 121 houses and six mosques are still remaining. Officials said the mosques would be demolished at the final stage of the project. What Is the Daalmandi project? The Daalmandi lane in Varanasi is being redeveloped as a model road project. Prime Minister Narendra Modi laid the foundation stone for the project during his 51st visit to Kashi. The Uttar Pradesh government has allocated Rs 215.88 crore for the project. Out of this, nearly Rs 191 crore will be paid as compensation to owners of 181 buildings and six mosques. 650-metre road to be expanded to 60 feet The Daalmandi stretch from Nai Sadak to Chowk Police Station is around 650 metres long. The proposal to widen the road to 17.5 metres (around 60 feet) has already been approved. The state government approved a budget of Rs 215 crore during the final day of the 2024-25 financial year, and Rs 2 crore has already been released. PWD teams conducted measurements of all 181 houses to determine how much of each property would fall under the widening project. Registry and compensation procedures have already begun. So far, registry formalities for 46 houses have been completed, and demolition work is being carried out gradually. Underground utilities planned under redevelopment According to PWD officials, the widened road will include a 30-foot-wide carriageway along with 15-foot-wide footpaths on both sides. Electricity lines, sewer systems, and water pipelines will be shifted underground as part of the redevelopment. Authorities also plan to remove the overhead network of hanging wires from the area.

stories.title: Vinesh Phogat says she's eligible to compete despite WFI ban:Wrestler says she will respond to federation's notice within 14 days
stories.summary: Wrestler Vinesh Phogat has responded to the show-cause notice from the Wrestling Federation of India (WFI), which barred her from competing in domestic tournaments until June 26. On Monday, Vinesh posted on social media saying that she had already received permission to play on 1 January. She claimed that the WFI had misunderstood her leave. She also said that she is eligible to participate in the Open Ranking Tournament being held in Gonda, Uttar Pradesh and has completed her registration for the same. The star wrestler also said did not violate doping rules and had already informed the officials about her non-participation in the tests. On 9 May, WFI had issued a show-cause notice to Vinesh on charges of indiscipline and violation of anti-doping rules. In the 15-page notice, WFI had written that Vinesh did not give six months' notice for her return from retirement. Therefore, she will not be able to play domestic competitions until 26 June. ‘WFI misunderstood the timelines’ In a note on social media, the 31-year-old said that the WFI misunderstood the timelines of my sabbatical from the sport and subsequent return to training and competitions. "I have been deemed eligible to return to official training and competition on January 1, 2026. I have official confirmation from the International Testing Agency (ITA)," a part of her note read. Vinesh also said that she would participate in the Senior Open Ranking Tournament being held in Gonda from 10 May to 12 May, 2026. She said she has registered her name for this and will make her comeback from retirement in this. Vinesh also opened up about the allegations of anti-doping rule violations that the WFI had slammed on her a few days ago in their notice. "With respect to the whereabouts failure from September 2024 and the Missed Test from December 2025, I confirm that I have co-operated with the relevant result management authorities promptly, and that both events do not amount to anti-doping rule violations per the National Anti-Doping Rules, 2021 or the WADA Code, 2021. ‘Will respond within 14 days’ Vinesh also addressed the topic of her participating in different weight categories at the 2024 selection trials in Patiala, stating that the ad-hoc committee running the WFI at that time was well-aware of the same and did not stop her from doing so. She said that she will prove her point and was looking forward to playing for India at the 2026 Asian Games and other international events. : Brijbhushan Singh's entry in wrestling, Vinesh Phogat out:War of words between wrestler and WFI former president intensifies| Video Official statement on Vinesh Phogat by WFI After the statement by Olympic wrestler Vinesh Phogat, Wrestling Federetion of India (WFI) shared an official response to Phogat. The organisation stated, " Vinesh Phogat was provided full security from the moment she arrived. As witnessed by everyone present, she met the officials and was informed about her ineligibility to participate, as per the rules and procedures in place. She freely interacted with the media and was not stopped or interrupted anywhere. Following this, she left the venue peacefully." “The Wrestling Federation of India treats every player equally, and player welfare and security remain our highest priorities. From her arrival in Gonda to her departure from the venue, complete security and support were extended to her at every step,” WFI added further. Why did WFI send notice to Vinesh Phogat? Did not give dope test on 18 December 2025 The International Testing Agency (ITA) had called wrestler Vinesh for a dope test in Bengaluru on 18 December, 2025, but she was not available at that time. Vinesh responded on 19 January, 2026, stating that she is a Congress MLA from Julana in Haryana. On 18 December, 2025, she was traveling from Bengaluru to Chandigarh to attend the winter session of the assembly. She also cited her new family responsibilities and the recent birth of her child. Due to her busy schedule, she was unable to update her location. Retirement at Paris Olympics, then talked about playing again Vinesh Phogat played her last wrestling match at the Paris Olympics in 2024. Vinesh played 3 matches in the 50 kg weight category on August 6, 2024, all on the same day. She defeated the Cuban wrestler in the semi-finals. Before playing the final, her weight was checked and found to be 100 grams over. She was subsequently disqualified. Vinesh Phogat announced her retirement from wrestling on 8 August, 2024. On 12 December 2025, Vinesh announced her return from retirement, stating that she wants to participate in the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

stories.title: Ballia’s Raj Singh arrested in Suvendu's PA murder case:Contested councillor elections; mother claims he is being framed
stories.summary: A suspected shooter from Uttar Pradesh has been arrested in connection with the murder of Chandranath Rath, personal assistant to Suvendu Adhikari. The accused, arrested from Ayodhya, is a resident of Ballia. In addition, West Bengal Police arrested two other suspected shooters, Mayank Raj Mishra and Vicky Maurya, from Buxar. Following the arrest, several details about the accused Raj Singh emerged. He had previously contested a council election. A poster linked to him also surfaced, in which he identified himself as the State General Secretary of the All India Kshatriya Mahasabha. His Facebook profile contains photographs with Minister Dayashankar Singh and a reel featuring former MP Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh. See 3 pictures- Raj’s mother claims SOG picked up her son Raj’s mother arrived at Ballia District Court on Monday afternoon and alleged that the Special Operations Group (SOG) had detained her son unlawfully. Crying before the media, she said, “On April 7, I travelled to Lucknow with my son for an MLC’s wedding. Raj, driver Om Prakash Singh, Raj’s friend Monu Singh and another person were with me. I stayed at a guesthouse near the wedding venue while the others attended the function.” She said the group returned after midnight and slept there. The next morning, they travelled to Kichhauchha Sharif in Ambedkar Nagar to offer prayers at Baba Makhdoom Ashraf shrine before heading to Ayodhya for darshan at Ram Lalla temple. ‘I met my son in the morning, then Bengal police took him away’ Jamwanti Singh claimed that while returning from Ayodhya, the SOG stopped their vehicle near a roadside dhaba. “They detained all of us, including the children. We were kept overnight at the women’s police station, while the others were held separately. The next morning I was allowed to meet Raj briefly, after which Bengal Police took him away on a flight. I do not know what happened afterwards,” she alleged. She added that Raj had also served as General Secretary of the Kshatriya Mahasabha and questioned why he was being implicated in the case. Lawyer alleges illegal arrest Raj Singh’s lawyer, Harivant Singh, addressed a press conference at the Ballia District Court premises on Monday. He claimed the arrest was illegal as no transit remand had been obtained. According to the lawyer, Raj was effectively abducted. Harivant Singh said CCTV footage showed Raj at his home on April 4, 5 and 6. “According to the information available to us, he has no connection with the Kolkata incident. Yet he has been linked to the murder case of the Chief Minister’s PA,” he said. The lawyer added that petitions were being submitted to the DIG, IG, DGP and the Governor of West Bengal, demanding an impartial investigation. He said, “No one can be detained and flown to another state without proper legal procedure.” Police suspect involvement of 8 people Investigating agencies suspect that at least eight people were involved in planning and carrying out the murder. According to preliminary findings, the accused conducted reconnaissance for several days before the attack. Investigators found that the attackers’ vehicle crossed Bali Toll Plaza shortly before the murder. A toll payment made via UPI helped police identify one suspect through the linked mobile number, eventually leading investigators to the remaining accused. Police are now matching CCTV footage from the toll plaza with images of the suspects and vehicles used in the crime. Officials said the accused had adopted multiple methods to conceal their identities and movements. Contract killers suspected, vehicles seized West Bengal Police suspect the murder may have been carried out by contract killers. Police said the nature of the operation suggested careful planning and the involvement of professional shooters. Investigators seized a car believed to have chased Rath’s Scorpio before the attack. The vehicle carried a fake registration number, while its chassis and engine numbers had been erased. Two motorcycles were also reportedly used in the attack. One bike was recovered near a tea stall around 4 km from the crime scene and was also found to have a fake registration number. The second motorcycle is yet to be traced. Chandranath had been associated with Suvendu since TMC days Before entering politics, Chandranath Rath had served in the Air Force. After taking voluntary retirement, he worked in the corporate sector for some time before joining political activities. He had been associated with Suvendu Adhikari since the latter’s days in the All India Trinamool Congress. Chandranath formally became part of Suvendu’s official team in 2019, when Suvendu was a minister in the government led by Mamata Banerjee. He was also involved in managing Suvendu’s election campaign in Bhabanipur, the constituency where Suvendu later defeated Mamata Banerjee by around 15,000 votes. Chandranath’s family also shifted from TMC to BJP Like Suvendu Adhikari, Chandranath’s family too was earlier associated with the Trinamool Congress. His mother, Hashi Rath, had held a post in the local panchayat body in Purba Medinipur during TMC rule. She joined the Bharatiya Janata Party along with Suvendu in 2020. Those close to Chandranath described him as calm and low-profile. He studied at Rahara Ramakrishna Mission and generally stayed away from public attention despite his long association with Suvendu. 90-minute timeline of the murder Police stated that such sophisticated weapons are not usually used by ordinary criminals, and the execution style pointed towards the involvement of professional shooters.

stories.title: No gas subsidy for income above ₹10 lakh:Supply resumes in Gorakhpur with 30% reduction from Motihari plant
stories.summary: Oil companies begin fresh subsidy scrutiny nationwide: LPG consumers earning above Rs 10 lakh may soon lose subsidy support Consumers already struggling to secure cooking gas cylinders are now facing another concern. After the confusion surrounding the mandatory Delivery Authentication Code (DAC) system, oil companies have begun tightening rules related to LPG subsidy eligibility. Families with an annual income of Rs 10 lakh or more may soon lose subsidy benefits on domestic cooking gas cylinders. The move is part of a fresh verification exercise being carried out using income tax records. Messages sent after income verification Oil companies have started identifying consumers whose declared family income crosses the prescribed limit. Consumers are receiving messages on their registered mobile numbers informing them that their subsidy may be discontinued. The message states that if they disagree with the decision, they must either: Contact the toll-free helpline 1800-2333-555 within seven days Register a complaint on the concerned oil company’s online portal Officials say subsidy benefits could be automatically stopped if no response is received within the stipulated period. What the notice to consumers says The message sent by oil companies clearly mentions that, according to income tax records, the taxable income of either the consumer or a family member exceeds Rs 10 lakh annually. As a result, the household may no longer remain eligible for subsidised LPG cylinders. Consumers have been given a seven-day window to raise objections or seek clarification. Existing subsidy structure remains limited At present, consumers in the state receive a subsidy of nearly Rs 59.05 on every 14.2-kg domestic LPG cylinder. Key details of the current subsidy system include: The subsidy structure has remained in place for several years. Supply disruptions continue across districts Even as subsidy rules tighten, the supply situation remains under pressure in eastern Uttar Pradesh. Cooking gas cylinders are now being supplied to Uttar Pradesh from the bottling plant in Motihari, Bihar. However, agencies say supply is still nearly 30 per cent lower than earlier levels. This has continued to create difficulties for both distributors and consumers. Some pressure has eased at the Indian Oil bottling plant in GIDA, Gorakhpur after supply resumed from Motihari. To manage demand, cylinders are also being dispatched to Basti district from the Lucknow bottling plant. Crisis persists despite partial restoration More than 75 gas agencies in Deoria, Kushinagar and Maharajganj districts earlier depended heavily on regular supply from the Motihari plant. Last month, supply to Uttar Pradesh agencies was abruptly halted, triggering a sharp cooking gas shortage across several districts. Consumers were forced to wait longer for cylinder deliveries, while agencies struggled to manage demand. Though supply has now resumed, the reduced allocation means relief remains limited. For consumers already dealing with delayed deliveries and stricter subsidy checks, the LPG crisis is far from over.

stories.title: 'Sanatan cannot be defeated', says CM Yogi:Claims India’s spiritual heritage endured while invaders faded away over time
stories.summary: Yogi Adityanath said in Kashi on Monday, ‘Those who tried to erase Sanatan have themselves turned to dust today. No one even remembers invaders such as Muhammad Ghori and Aurangzeb. Both Somnath and Kashi send a message from history that Sanatan culture may be attacked, but it can never be defeated. Destruction is temporary, while creation is eternal.’ Earlier, Anandiben Patel and the Chief Minister offered prayers at Shri Kashi Vishwanath Dham. They chanted ‘Om’ within the temple complex. The CM presented the Governor with a stole and a Rudraksha rosary. Both leaders also watched the live telecast of Narendra Modi performing ‘Jalabhishek’ at the Somnath Temple in Gujarat. The occasion marked 75 years since the reconstruction of the Somnath Temple. On May 11, 1951, the newly rebuilt temple was consecrated in independent India. The Somnath Amrit Mahotsav is being celebrated to commemorate the occasion. A programme was also organised in Kashi, where male and female students performed conch-blowing and damru recitals. Women who arrived from Gujarat raised slogans in support of PM Modi. See pictures- CM Yogi’s 5 key remarks 1. ‘Aurangzeb demolished the Vishwanath Temple’ The Chief Minister said that from Muhammad Ghori to the Mughals, several foreign invaders attempted to destroy India’s spiritual and cultural identity. He said Aurangzeb demolished the ancient temple of Baba Vishwanath and built what he described as “a structure of slavery” in its place. However, he added that they could not break the soul of India. According to the CM, Sanatan does not merely exist within temple walls, but in India’s collective consciousness. He said India’s spiritual philosophy regards the soul as immortal and eternal, which forms the foundation of the country’s cultural heritage. 2. ‘Kashi Vishwanath and Somnath are symbols of India’s pride’ Yogi said both Kashi Vishwanath Dham and Somnath Temple are symbols of India’s pride. He said the divine and grand form of Kashi Vishwanath Dham is now visible in Kashi, while Somnath Temple is once again reflecting India’s glory with renewed radiance. The CM also alleged that even today there are forces that do not wish to see India’s spiritual and cultural centres progress. Referring to opposition faced during the reconstruction efforts, he said some groups had objected to the re-consecration ceremony of Somnath Temple and had similarly attempted to obstruct the construction of the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya. 3. ‘Invaders tried to destroy Somnath’s glory’ The Chief Minister said that around 1,000 years ago, foreign invaders including Mahmud of Ghazni attacked the Somnath Temple 17 times in an attempt to destroy its glory. He said the invaders believed that by destroying idols and looting the temple’s wealth, they could permanently extinguish India’s spirit. According to him, such attacks were not limited to Somnath, but targeted thousands of religious sites across the country, including Kashi Vishwanath Dham. 4. ‘Earlier governments lacked commitment towards sanatan traditions’ CM Yogi said that after independence, India had an opportunity to strongly promote its Sanatan traditions and cultural heritage, but at the time there was no ideological commitment towards India’s civilisational identity and Sanatan values. He said that under PM Modi’s leadership, the country has received a new direction. As a result, traditions and values that foreign invaders attempted to destroy nearly a thousand years ago are now being restored with dignity and respect. He described the ongoing celebrations marking 75 years of Somnath Temple’s re-establishment as an example of this transformation. 5. ‘India’s temples symbolise eternity’ The CM said that despite opposition from the government of that era, India’s first President, Rajendra Prasad, visited Gujarat for the Somnath ceremony. Referring to Rajendra Prasad’s remarks, Yogi said physical structures may be damaged temporarily, but invaders failed to understand that the soul of India is timeless and immortal. He concluded by saying that India’s temples stand as enduring symbols of that eternity.

stories.title: Storm, rain alert in UP from tomorrow:Hail likely, Prayagraj remains hottest at 39.6°C
stories.summary: The spell of storms and rain in UP has been paused for a week. Monday morning, the weather in Eastern UP is clear. Bright sunshine has emerged. Clouds have covered Saharanpur, Muzaffarnagar, and Shamli in Western UP. The weather in the Bundelkhand districts is normal. There is no storm-rain alert anywhere in the entire state on Monday. From tomorrow, that is Tuesday, the weather is expected to deteriorate again. According to the Meteorological Department, a new western disturbance is becoming active. Its effect will start from May 12. During this time, there may be storms and rain. Hail may also fall. Winds will also blow at a speed of 30 to 40. Due to no rain, there has been a rapid increase in temperature. On Sunday, the day temperature reached 40°C. Prayagraj remained the hottest city. Here, the mercury was recorded at 39.6°C. Lucknow weather scientist Atul Kumar Singh said- Due to the activation of western disturbance, the weather will deteriorate between May 12 and 15. There will be rain with strong winds. The temperature will see a slight drop due to the rain. But after this, an increase of 6 to 8 °C in temperature can be recorded. This means the mercury in most cities will cross 45 °C. See pictures- Why is there fluctuation in the weather? The Meteorological Department says that the weather in the mountains of Uttarakhand is continuously changing. There is snowfall in some places and rain in others. On some days, the weather is clearing up with sunshine. Such fluctuations are expected for the next few days. Its effect is visible in UP. The winds coming from the mountains are keeping the weather cold. They are creating systems favorable for rain. What will the weather be like for the next 3 days? Forecast of less rainfall in monsoon this year Private weather agency Skymet Weather has released the forecast for this year's monsoon. According to this, monsoon rainfall may be 6% less than normal. The normal average rainfall in the country during the 4 months of monsoon from June to September is 868.6 mm. Less than normal monsoon means that rainfall will be between 90% to 95%. The agency has predicted 94% rainfall. There will be normal rainfall in June, but the decline will start from July, and the monsoon will weaken in August and September. Especially in August-September, there are indications of a greater rainfall deficit. Question- What should be done to avoid heatstroke? Answer- In summer, just avoiding the sun is not enough, but adopting the right habits is equally important. A little caution can prevent a serious problem like heatstroke. There will be less rainfall during monsoon in UP too, know the reason Between June and September, Uttar Pradesh is also expected to receive below-normal rainfall. Dr. M Mahapatra, Director General of the Meteorological Department, stated that this year there are signs of La Niña-like conditions ending in the Pacific Ocean and moving towards El Niño, which will cause reduced rainfall. This means there are indications that the southwest monsoon will be weaker than normal this year. Additionally, the reduced snow formation in the Northern Hemisphere during January-March this year may also affect the monsoon. Know about El Niño and La Niña

stories.title: Retired Army man turns psycho killer in UP:3 murders in 26 hours; 2 youths shot on moving trains, woman killed in hospital
stories.summary: A suspected psychopathic killer has been arrested in Chandauli. The accused, believed to be around 45 years old, is a retired Army personnel. He allegedly carried out three murders within 26 and a half hours. In all three cases, the victims were shot in the temple at close range, leaving them with virtually no chance of survival. The first killing took place around 7 am on Sunday aboard the DDU–Tadighat passenger train, where a young man was shot dead. The second occurred at about 2 am on Sunday near Mughalsarai Railway Station, inside the Jammu Tawi Express train. The third murder was reported at around 8:30 am on Monday in Chandauli, where the accused allegedly entered a private hospital and shot a woman lying on a bed by pressing a pistol against her temple. The three crime scenes were located within a radius of nearly 20 to 25 kilometres. Police officials identified the accused as Gurpreet Singh alias Virendra, a resident of Amritsar. Investigators believe he was responsible for all three murders. During the investigation, police concluded that the accused fits the profile of a psychopathic serial killer. After the hospital shooting, he was apprehended while attempting to flee. Police recovered two pistols from his possession, one legally registered in his name and another allegedly an illegal firearm. Incident details Accused also tried to shoot the staff Dr. Sunil Kumar Gautam, director of Jeevak Hospital, said that this morning, a person with his face covered came to the hospital on the pretext of getting treatment. During this, the staff nurse noticed his suspicious movements and sent a ward boy. Meanwhile, the accused entered the ward of admitted patients and shot a woman there. The accused also tried to shoot the staff, but people managed to save their lives by hiding under the beds. After this, the accused fled the hospital, brandishing a weapon. However, villagers chased and caught him and handed him over to the police. SP Akash Patel said- Apart from the weapon, 10 thousand rupees in cash have been recovered from the accused. Currently, the identity of the accused has not been ascertained. He is being interrogated. The case will be revealed soon.

stories.title: Bihar man shot dead on Jammu-Tawi Express:Body dumped on tracks between Mughalsarai Varanasi railway stations
stories.summary: A 42-year-old man from Bihar’s Gaya district was shot dead inside a moving train in Uttar Pradesh’s Varanasi district in the early hours of Monday. The victim, identified as Dinesh Shah, was travelling with his wife aboard the Kolkata-Jammu Tavi Express when gunmen opened fire at close range. Police said the attackers shot Shah in the head moments after he stepped out of the toilet around 2 am. The incident triggered panic inside the coach as terrified passengers rushed out after hearing the gunshot. Attackers escape as train slows down The murder took place nearly 3 km before Mughalsarai railway station near Block Hut-B. Officials said the train had slowed down in the section, allowing the attackers to jump off and flee before railway police could reach the spot. Passengers immediately alerted the Railway Protection Force and Government Railway Police. By 2:42 am, the train reached Varanasi Junction, where Shah’s body was taken off the coach for investigation and postmortem procedures. Family travelling to pilgrimage town Dinesh Shah, a resident of Pipariya village in Bihar’s Gaya district, was travelling to Naimisharanya in Sitapur with family members. Travel details: According to police, Shah’s wife rushed to the spot after hearing the gunshot and found him lying in a pool of blood inside the coach passage. Cash and jewellery found untouched Investigators said robbery may not have been the immediate motive behind the killing. Police recovered: A police team continued travelling with the train to question passengers and gather clues about the attackers. Another team has been sent to Shah’s village in Bihar to speak with relatives and examine possible personal angles behind the murder. Similar train murder reported a day earlier The incident comes barely a day after another passenger was shot dead aboard a train in the same region. According to police, a man identified as Mangru from Ghazipur was murdered on Sunday morning while travelling in a passenger train from Pandit Deendayal Upadhyay Junction towards Dildarnagar and Tarighat. Officials said the attackers placed a pistol on his temple before shooting him dead and fleeing with his bag near Sakaldiha railway station. Police probe raises security concerns The back-to-back killings inside moving trains have raised serious concerns over passenger safety on railway routes passing through eastern Uttar Pradesh. Sakaldiha Circle Officer Krishnamurari Sharma said investigators are examining all possible angles, including targeted killing and prior enmity. Railway police are now scanning passenger details, questioning witnesses and trying to identify whether the attackers boarded the train with Shah as targets already fixed.

stories.title: SP may reduce Muslim candidates in 2027 polls:Akhilesh reshapes public image through religious visits; to follow pandits' advice
stories.summary: Ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav is trying to change his political image. The SP has long been seen as a party focused mainly on Muslim and Yadav voters, while the BJP has often targeted this perception during elections. Now, Akhilesh is attempting to create a new image by building the Kedareshwar temple in Etawah. He also claims that he plans his daily routine according to the advice of priests and astrologers. Political experts believe the SP may give more importance to upper caste leaders in the 2027 elections instead of relying heavily on Muslim candidates. This political shift in the SP has become more visible after the heavy defeat of the Trinamool Congress in the West Bengal elections. First, let's understand Akhilesh's image, which he inherited As soon as he took over the party, Akhilesh managed Muslim, Yadav voters Akhilesh Yadav inherited this image. After ordering firing on karsevaks in Ayodhya in 1990, the BJP started calling Mulayam Singh 'Mullah Mulayam'. After this, SP's identity became based on the Muslim-Yadav (M-Y) equation. When Akhilesh took over the party's command, he was seen as the protector of this very vote bank. Muzaffarnagar riots, BJP's allegations - soft stance for a particular community The Muzaffarnagar riots of 2013, during Akhilesh's tenure as Chief Minister, further strengthened this image. The SP government had issued a notification to provide compensation of Rs 5 lakh each only to riot-affected Muslims. This decision had to be withdrawn after the intervention of the Supreme Court. The BJP had alleged that the Akhilesh government adopted a soft stance towards the Muslim community. In March 2014, the Supreme Court also acknowledged that the government had largely failed to prevent the violence. After the Muzaffarnagar riots, a message went among Hindus that the SP government was biased towards Muslims. Now an attempt to change the image Kedareswar being built on the lines of Kedarnath Akhilesh Yadav is building 'Shri Kedareswar Mahadev Temple' in Etawah on the lines of Kedarnath temple in Uttarakhand. Akhilesh is the chief trustee of the temple. The temple is being built on the 'Shivshakti Aksh Rekha', which makes it religiously significant. Senior journalist Akhilesh Bajpai says - There is a plan to inaugurate this temple in the election year. Through this, Akhilesh wants to break the BJP's narrative, in which he is portrayed as anti-Hindu or only a benefactor of Muslims. Building a temple like Kedarnath is clearly part of a strategy to respond to BJP's Hindutva agenda. It is a different matter that Akhilesh has avoided visiting the two main Hindu temples in UP, Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi (Mathura) and Ram Mandir (Ayodhya). However, he did go for a Ganga bath during the Mahakumbh. Strategy to be decided on the suggestion of pundits and astrologers Akhilesh's press conference on May 6 surprised everyone in political circles. He had said, "Now I am taking every step on 'Pandit ji's' advice. In 2012, my government was formed under the guidance of Pandits and astrologers. Now I am walking on the same path again." Senior journalist Siddharth Kalhans says, "Akhilesh is saying that when to leave home, what color to wear, and even when to start election campaigning, all this will be decided by his astrologers." Through this, Akhilesh is trying to appease the Brahmin community. He is presenting himself as a protector of Sanatani traditions by raising issues like the insult of Brahmins and Shankaracharya. Expansion of PDA beyond the Muslim-Yadav factor Senior journalist Akhilesh Bajpai says - Akhilesh has understood that it is no longer easy to reach power in UP with the help of the Muslim-Yadav (M-Y) equation. Until the 2022 assembly elections, SP's focus remained on this equation, but they lost. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, Akhilesh gave the slogan of 'PDA' (Pichda, Dalit, Alpasankhyak - Backward, Dalit, Minority). By giving fewer tickets to Yadavs and Muslims, he bet on other backward castes and Dalits. This experiment was quite successful. BJP suffered a major dent and SP emerged as the largest party in UP. Now Akhilesh is expanding this formula in 2027. He is resorting to soft Hindutva to include upper castes in it. Possibility of major upheaval in ticket distribution Sources associated with SP say that the number of Muslim candidates may be reduced in the 2027 assembly elections. In the 2024 elections, out of SP's 62 candidates, only 4 were Muslim. The same formula may be applied in 2027 as well. Akhilesh believes that fielding more Muslim candidates will make it easier for BJP to polarize the elections. By giving fewer tickets to the Muslim community and associating himself with temples and Brahmins, Akhilesh is trying to breach a strong fortress of BJP. However, this strategy is also risky, as minority votes might scatter if tickets are reduced. Owaisi-Mayawati can harm SP Siddharth Kalahans says - The biggest challenge in front of Akhilesh's new strategy is Asaduddin Owaisi and Mayawati. If SP distances itself from the Muslim community or gives them fewer tickets, then Owaisi's AIMIM and BSP will try to fill this void. Owaisi has caused similar damage to opposition parties in Bihar, Maharashtra and Bengal. The direct benefit of scattered Muslim votes goes to BJP. BJP's New Strategy to Corner After the 2024 Victory Senior journalist Akhilesh Bajpai states - BJP had suffered losses in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. To compensate for the losses incurred due to the narrative of changing the constitution and the slogan of '400 paar' (crossing 400 seats), BJP is now working more aggressively at the booth level. However, the circumstances of the Lok Sabha elections were different. There, SP benefited from BJP's strategic mistakes, but assembly elections are fought on local issues. This is why Akhilesh is now establishing himself as a leader of all communities. Taking the help of astrology and giving importance to Brahmins is an attempt to break BJP's strategy to corner. Meanwhile, Siddharth Kalahans believes that Akhilesh's path of soft Hindutva is both his political compulsion and a well-thought-out strategy. UP has now become the center of polarized politics, where the contest is directly between SP and BJP. Amidst Mayawati's declining support base, Akhilesh is presenting himself as the only alternative to the BJP. Through building temples, astrologers' advice, and new ticket equations, he is hoping for a return to power in 2027. This strategy is quite different from 2022. Because now Akhilesh is not just doing politics of opposition, but is on the path of countering BJP's agenda in his own way. It will be interesting to see whether UP likes SP's 'new avatar' or not?

stories.title: Shah fulfils promise by making Manoj Pandey minister:Yogi cabinet filled to full strength for first time, OBC ministers rise to 25
stories.summary: The Yogi Adityanath government carried out its second cabinet expansion on Sunday, filling all 60 ministerial posts for the first time in the Chief Minister’s nine-year tenure. The reshuffle is being viewed as the BJP’s final political groundwork ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. The expansion rewarded loyal leaders, addressed caste equations and attempted to strengthen the BJP’s support base across Purvanchal, Western UP, Awadh and Bundelkhand. Through the induction of OBC, Dalit and regional leaders, the BJP also tried to counter the Samajwadi Party’s PDA formula, 'Pichda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak' (Backward, Dalit and Minority). BJP counters Akhilesh Yadav’s PDA strategy The Samajwadi Party has been trying to unite backward classes and Dalits under its PDA campaign. To respond to this, the BJP included three OBC faces and two Dalit leaders in the cabinet expansion. The BJP wants to send a message that backward and Dalit communities are not only being respected but are also getting a fair share in power. The party believes this move will strengthen its hold among caste groups that could otherwise shift towards the SP. After the expansion, the number of OBC ministers increased from 22 to 25. General category ministers rose from 21 to 22. The number of Brahmin ministers increased from seven to eight, while Dalit ministers rose from eight to ten. The cabinet also includes one Sikh, one Muslim and one Scheduled Tribe minister. Cabinet expansion after more than 2 years This is the first cabinet expansion in more than two years. Political experts believe there has been no major ideological change, but the BJP has clearly focused on caste and regional representation. The reshuffle also reflects continuity in the party’s social engineering strategy. Bhupendra Chaudhary returns to cabinet Jat leader Bhupendra Chaudhary has been rewarded for maintaining close ties with the BJP’s central leadership. Chaudhary was made BJP state president in 2022 and had stepped down from his ministerial role at that time. He has now returned to the cabinet. In Western UP, Chaudhary is considered one of the BJP’s strongest Jat leaders. Unlike senior Jat minister Laxmi Narayan Chaudhary, who has earlier been associated with several parties including the SP, BSP, Congress and RLD, Bhupendra Chaudhary is seen as a core BJP cadre leader. He earlier served as Minister of State for PWD in Yogi Adityanath’s first term and was later promoted as Panchayati Raj Minister in 2019. In the second Yogi government, he again handled the Panchayati Raj portfolio before becoming the BJP state president on August 25, 2022. He remained state president until December 14, 2025. With his inclusion, the Yogi cabinet now has three Jat ministers, Bhupendra Chaudhary, Sugarcane Development Minister Laxmi Narayan Chaudhary and Minister of State KP Malik. Amit Shah keeps promise to Manoj Pandey The induction of Manoj Pandey is being seen as the fulfilment of a promise made by Union Home Minister Amit Shah. Pandey, formerly an SP MLA from Unchahar, rebelled during the Rajya Sabha elections in February 2024. He voted in favour of the BJP and reportedly helped six other SP MLAs support the party as well. At the time, Amit Shah had assured him of a ministerial role in the UP government. During the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, Shah shared the stage with Manoj Pandey in Raebareli, where Pandey formally joined the BJP. Shah had also visited his residence. BJP strengthens Brahmin representation Manoj Pandey is considered an influential Brahmin face in both Awadh and Purvanchal. He has often spoken openly for Brahmin rights and publicly opposed controversial remarks made by former minister Swami Prasad Maurya against Brahmins and Sanatan Dharma. The BJP believes his inclusion could reduce dissatisfaction among Brahmin voters in Awadh and eastern UP. The move also sends a message that Brahmin dissatisfaction did not damage the BJP politically. Earlier, Jitin Prasada had represented the Brahmin quota in the state cabinet before being moved to the Centre after becoming an MP from Pilibhit. The BJP now has three prominent Brahmin faces in UP politics, Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak, Union Minister of State Jitin Prasada and newly inducted minister Manoj Pandey. Lodh community given greater representation The BJP also addressed concerns within the Lodh community. Leaders such as Dharampal Singh, BL Verma and Rajveer Singh, son of former CM Kalyan Singh, were considered contenders for BJP state president. However, the party eventually appointed Kurmi leader Pankaj Chaudhary. This reportedly created resentment among Lodh leaders, who argued that Kurmis had stronger representation in government. To balance this, Kailash Rajput from the Lodh community was inducted as minister. The cabinet now has three Lodh ministers, Dharampal Singh, Sandeep Singh and Kailash Rajput. Vishwakarma Community gets representation Hansraj Vishwakarma, a close aide of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and former BJP district president in Varanasi, has also been made a minister. The Vishwakarma community has a sizeable presence in UP but previously lacked cabinet representation. With his inclusion, there are now four ministers from Varanasi in the Yogi cabinet, Anil Rajbhar, Ravindra Jaiswal, Dayashankar Mishra Dayalu and Hansraj Vishwakarma. BJP plays ‘Pasi Woman Card’ The BJP also attempted to strengthen its Dalit and women's outreach by inducting Krishna Paswan. The Pasi community has long been seen as a BJP support base. Party leaders reportedly feared the vote bank could weaken if the community did not receive stronger representation before 2027. By appointing Krishna Paswan, the BJP believes it has simultaneously addressed Dalit, Pasi and women representation. Valmiki Community strengthened further The BJP also strengthened its outreach among Valmiki voters by appointing Surendra Diler as minister. The Valmiki community is considered an important BJP support base among Dalits. After former minister Anoop Valmiki became an MP from Hathras, the Khair Assembly by-election was won by Surendra Diler, son of late MP Rajiv Diler. His induction ensures continued Valmiki representation in the cabinet. 2 ministers promoted Ajit Pal Singh and Somendra Tomar were promoted as Ministers of State (Independent Charge). Ajit Pal Singh’s promotion is aimed at retaining support from the Pal community, which both the SP and BSP are trying to attract. Somendra Tomar’s elevation comes as the SP attempts to strengthen support among Gurjars in Western UP. Women still underrepresented Despite Krishna Paswan’s induction, women remain underrepresented in the cabinet. The Yogi government now has six women ministers out of 60, making women’s representation just 10%. The women ministers include Baby Rani Maurya, Gulab Devi, Rajni Tiwari, Pratibha Shukla, Vijay Lakshmi Gautam and Krishna Paswan. Youngest cabinet so far The current cabinet is younger than Yogi Adityanath’s first government. In 2022, the average age of ministers was 55 years. It has now dropped to 52.8 years. Surendra Diler, aged 33, is the youngest minister in the cabinet, while Dr Arun Kumar Saxena, aged around 74, is the oldest.

stories.title: Bike crashes into truck in Bulandshahar:Husband, wife and 3 children die, family was returning from relatives’ house
stories.summary: Five members of a family, including a husband, wife and their three children, were killed after their motorcycle rammed into the rear of a truck in Bulandshahr on Friday evening. The accident took place around 5:30 pm on National Highway-34 in the Dehat Kotwali area. Following the incident, the truck driver fled from the spot with the vehicle. According to police, Uttam Singh (45), a resident of Dhameda Keerat village, had borrowed a motorcycle to visit relatives in Khurja. He had reportedly told the owner that he would return after completing some work. His wife Urmila (40) and their three children, Nishant (8), Disha (6) and Anayra (4), were travelling with him on the same motorcycle. The family was returning home after meeting relatives when the accident occurred. First, see two pictures Motorcycle crashed into truck after it slowed suddenly Police said a truck travelling ahead near Bhaisauli Cut was moving at around 70 kmph when it suddenly slowed down. Uttam Singh’s motorcycle, which was reportedly travelling at high speed behind the truck, lost balance and crashed into the rear of the vehicle. The impact threw the entire family onto the road. Eyewitnesses said the bodies of the husband, wife and children were found piled on top of one another, while the motorcycle lay nearby with its front portion badly damaged. Uttam Singh worked in a private company Uttam Singh was employed at a private company in Secunderabad. He had travelled to Khurja to meet relatives and had borrowed the motorcycle from an acquaintance for the trip. Their eldest son Nishant studied in Class 3, daughter Disha in Class 2, while youngest daughter Anayra was studying in Class 1. The family includes Uttam Singh’s parents, brother, sister-in-law and sister. Police informed the relatives about the accident, though family members had not reached the spot immediately after the incident. SSP and senior officers reached accident site After receiving information, Senior Superintendent of Police Dinesh Kumar Singh, SP City Abhishek Pratap and CO City Prakhar Pandey reached the scene. Police shifted all five victims to hospital, where doctors declared them brought dead. Truck seized, driver absconding Following the crash, the truck driver attempted to flee with the vehicle. Police chased the truck, after which the driver abandoned it and escaped. SSP Dinesh Kumar Singh said the truck bears a Haryana registration number and has been seized by police. He added that all five bodies have been sent for post-mortem examination and efforts are underway to arrest the driver.

stories.title: 2 youths die inside septic tank in Lucknow:One enters first for cleaning, second follows him after seeing no activity
stories.summary: Two labourers died while cleaning a septic tank in Lucknow on Friday afternoon. The incident took place in Navipanah village under the Mal police station area, around 35 km from the district headquarters. According to initial information, labourer Rinku first entered the septic tank for cleaning work. When there was no sound or movement from him for a long time, another labourer, Rajesh, went inside the tank to check on him. However, no response was received from either of them afterwards, triggering panic among people present at the spot. Villagers and police pulled both out unconscious Locals immediately informed the Dial 112 police. With the help of the police team and villagers, both labourers were pulled out of the tank in an unconscious condition. They were rushed to hospital, where doctors declared both of them dead. See 3 pictures- Poisonous gas suspected inside tank Police suspect that poisonous gas inside the septic tank may have caused both labourers to lose consciousness, leading to their deaths. However, officials said the exact cause of death will only be confirmed after the post-mortem report is received. Following the incident, grief spread among the families of the deceased. Inspector Nawab Ahmed of Mal police station said- Two labourers died while cleaning a septic tank. It is suspected that there was some poisonous gas in the tank, due to which both labourers lost their lives.

stories.title: UP Evening Wrap:Cracks emerge in Taj Mahal’s Royal Gate after storms and heavy rain; Suvendu named new CM of West Bengal
stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest news from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines- 1. Suvendu Adhikari elected new Chief Minister of West Bengal The BJP legislature party elected Suvendu Adhikari as the next Chief Minister of West Bengal during a meeting in Kolkata. Union Home Minister Amit Shah formally announced his name after the party’s victory. 2. Akhilesh meets Mamata and Stalin, says allies are not abandoned in difficult times SP chief Akhilesh Yadav met Mamata Banerjee in Kolkata and reiterated support to alliance partners after the election results. He later shared photographs with Mamata and Tamil Nadu CM Stalin. 3. Cracks emerge in Taj Mahal’s Royal Gate after storms and heavy rain Visible deterioration has appeared at the Taj Mahal’s historic Royal Gate, with cracks developing and stones shifting from their original positions. The damage reportedly worsened following recent storms and rainfall. 4. TVK set to form government in Tamil Nadu, Vijay likely to be next CM Support from Congress, VCK, CPI and CPI(M) has reportedly strengthened Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam’s numbers after the Assembly election results. Vijay now appears poised to lead the next government in the state. 5. UP government orders conversion of prepaid smart meters into postpaid system The Uttar Pradesh government has directed power departments to convert prepaid electricity meters into postpaid meters. Consumers will also be allowed to clear pending bills till April in ten instalments. 6. Police encounters of child-crime accused raise questions over emerging pattern in UP Within hours of a child rape and murder case in Hardoi, police shot dead the accused in an encounter. The incident marks the third such police killing involving crimes against children in Uttar Pradesh within a month. 7. Iran seizes oil tanker, accuses vessel of disrupting country’s oil exports Iran has seized an oil tanker amid rising tensions with the United States despite claims of a ceasefire remaining in effect. The US military also carried out retaliatory strikes targeting sites linked to attacks on its forces. 8. Prayagraj girl’s skeletal remains found 17 days after alleged murder by boyfriend The skeletal remains of a Class 9 student were recovered from a bushy area in Prayagraj more than two weeks after she allegedly died. Police suspect her 17-year-old boyfriend was involved in the murder. 9. Smart meter backlash may trigger UP cabinet reshuffle, AK Sharma under pressure Public anger over prepaid smart electricity meters has reportedly forced the UP government to reconsider its policy. BJP and RSS leaders are said to have warned the issue could hurt the party electorally. 10. Centre plans major overhaul of 15 lakh government schools from May 2026 The Centre is preparing sweeping reforms aimed at strengthening governance in government schools across India. School Management Committees and parents may get greater control over budgets and expenditure decisions.

stories.title: 'We do not abandon allies in difficult times':Akhilesh meets Mamata and Stalin after election results, shares photos
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav met outgoing chief minister Mamata Banerjee during a courtesy visit to her Kolkata residence on Thursday. Reiterating his continued support to her, Yadav said he or his party never abandon allies during difficult times. “We are not the ones who abandon people in difficult times,” Akhilesh said. The UP leader also shared photographs of his meetings with Mamata and M.K. Stalin in a X post. Akhilesh last met Stalin during an INDIA alliance meeting ahead of the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. Mamata received Akhilesh at the gate When Akhilesh reached Mamata’s residence, Mamata herself came to the gate to receive him. As Akhilesh moved forward to present her with a shawl, Mamata said, “What was the need for this?” To this, Akhilesh replied, “Didi, you fought, you have not lost.” Om Prakash Rajbhar takes a dig Reacting to the meeting, Uttar Pradesh minister Om Prakash Rajbhar mocked the two leaders. He said Akhilesh had gone to console Mamata by saying, “You have lost only once, while we have lost twice. Let us come together and begin a new series of defeats.” Rajbhar also claimed that when the Bengal election results were being declared, Akhilesh remained silent for four hours and only later decided to meet Mamata. First, see photos that Akhilesh posted- Mamata had earlier refused the visit Akhilesh was initially scheduled to visit Bengal on May 5, immediately after the election results were announced. However, Mamata reportedly asked him not to come at that time. Although Akhilesh did not campaign in the Bengal elections, he continued supporting Mamata through social media posts during the campaign period. First meeting after election defeat This was the first meeting between Mamata and any INDIA alliance leader after the Trinamool Congress defeat in the Bengal elections. Before this, Mamata and Akhilesh had last met on January 27. Political observers consider the renewed interaction between the Samajwadi Party and Trinamool Congress significant ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. 2 pictures of Mamata-Akhilesh meeting- TMC and DMK suffered major defeats In West Bengal, the BJP won 207 seats, while the Trinamool Congress was reduced to 80 seats. Compared with the 2021 elections, the BJP’s vote share increased by around 8%. Out of 119 seats that the TMC had consistently won for the past 15 years, the BJP captured 75 seats. This means the TMC lost nearly 63% of its traditional strongholds. Meanwhile, in Tamil Nadu, actor Vijay’s TVK secured 108 seats, while the DMK won 59 seats and the AIADMK secured 47. What does Akhilesh’s post indicate? Political analysts believe Akhilesh Yadav is trying to send a message of opposition unity by publicly standing with both Mamata Banerjee and MK Stalin. Senior journalist Rajendra Kumar said Akhilesh’s political style shows that once he aligns with someone, he generally avoids publicly attacking them, even after failed alliances. He pointed to the 2017 alliance between the Samajwadi Party and Congress, which performed poorly in elections. Despite the setback, Akhilesh did not make statements against Congress that could damage relations between the parties. The same pattern was seen after the 2019 alliance with Mayawati. Even after the alliance collapsed, Akhilesh refrained from criticising either Mayawati or the BSP. Rajendra Kumar added that Akhilesh’s restraint helped him gain support among Scheduled Caste voters. He also noted that even after the successful opposition alliance in the 2024 elections, several Congress leaders made controversial remarks against Akhilesh and the Samajwadi Party. Despite this, neither Akhilesh nor his party leaders responded aggressively. According to Rajendra Kumar, Akhilesh is attempting to project himself as a major opposition face who maintains cordial relations with all opposition parties, making him acceptable as a future national leader if such an opportunity arises. BJP says ‘Sad people met to wipe each other’s tears’ BJP leaders strongly criticised the meeting between Akhilesh and Mamata-

stories.title: Crack emerges in Taj Mahal’s historic Royal Gate:Stones fall from monument during storms and rain
stories.summary: The Taj Mahal, regarded as one of the most beautiful monuments in the world, is now showing visible signs of deterioration. The Royal Gate, also known as the Shahi Darwaza, has developed cracks in several places, while many stones have shifted from their original positions. The condition of the gate has become so fragile that it is no longer able to withstand storms and heavy rain. During recent spells of bad weather, stones from the structure broke off and fell twice. On several occasions, tourists narrowly escaped injury. This is not the first such incident. In recent years, stones, railings and jalis across different sections of the Taj Mahal complex have also collapsed or broken due to weakening structures and weather damage. Recent incidents at the Taj Mahal April 7, 2026- A powerful storm and heavy rain struck Agra. During the storm, white and red stones from the Royal Gate came loose and fell. Fortunately, no tourists were injured. April 30, 2026- Even a comparatively mild storm and rainfall proved too much for the weakened structure of the Royal Gate. Five pieces of white stone broke off and fell to the ground. Earlier incidents May 31, 2024- A stone from the Royal Gate broke and fell. December 20, 2024- Stones detached and fell from the wall of the Southern Gate of the Taj Mahal complex. May 29, 2020- Marble and red sandstone jalis in the Taj Mahal complex were damaged and broken. During the same incident, the Western Gate became tilted after one of its hinges broke. These incidents are only a few examples. Stones and lattice structures at the monument have reportedly broken and fallen multiple times over the years. Royal Gate in dilapidated condition The Royal Gate, considered the main entrance to the Taj Mahal, is now visibly deteriorating. Stones have loosened in several areas, while cracks can clearly be seen across sections of the walls. Many stones have weakened with age and are gradually detaching from the structure. The red sandstone gate also contains white and black stones used for decorative carvings, many of which are now falling out. In several places, gaps have formed in the walls where stones have collapsed. White and black decorative stones have also started coming loose from the structure. 4 pictures of the dilapidated Royal Gate- History of the Royal Gate The Royal Gate serves as the principal entrance to the Taj Mahal complex. After entering through the eastern or western gates, visitors reach the forecourt and then proceed to the main mausoleum through this gate. Earlier, tourists entering through the southern gate also approached the monument through the Royal Gate. However, the southern gate has remained closed since 2018. Historians believe the Royal Gate is as old as the main mausoleum itself and was constructed during the same phase of development. What historians and experts say ? Historian Rajkishore Raje said the Royal Gate was built alongside the main mausoleum during the Mughal era. At that time, it was known as the Shahi Darwaza. During British rule, it later came to be called the Royal Gate. SK Kulshrestha, former in-charge of the Taj Mahal and a retired Conservation Assistant with the Archaeological Survey of India, said the stones have naturally weakened with age. According to him, unless high-quality conservation work is carried out, stones will continue to crack and fall. He explained that conservation work was earlier handled directly by the department, with engineers carefully considering the monument’s historical characteristics. However, most restoration work is now contractor-driven. He believes contractors often lack the specialised expertise required for heritage conservation, which has affected the quality of repair work. Kulshrestha also pointed to the unavailability of traditional construction materials as a major concern. Earlier conservation work used pebble lime and specially prepared mortar containing strengthening compounds. Such materials are now difficult to obtain. Taj Mahal generates more than Rs 100 crore annually Despite repeated increases in ticket prices, tourist interest in the Taj Mahal remains extremely high. The monument continues to generate the highest revenue among sites protected by the Archaeological Survey of India. At present- An additional Rs 200 ticket is required to enter the main dome area. As a result, Indian visitors spend Rs 250 to view the complete monument, while foreign tourists pay Rs 1,300. Know the income for each year According to ASI data, offline ticket sales alone generated Rs 105 crore 49 lakh 12 thousand 855 during the financial years 2024-25 and 2025-26 combined. Including online ticket sales, the total revenue exceeded Rs 200 crore. Even after ticket prices increased over the decades, from just 20 paise to Rs 250 for Indian visitors, tourist numbers have not seen any major decline. Ticket system introduced in 1966 Entry to the Taj Mahal remained completely free until 1966. That year, a ticketing system was introduced for the first time, with tickets priced at just 20 paise. Today, a tiered pricing structure is followed to regulate the growing number of tourists, with separate rates for different categories of visitors. How ticket prices increased Concerns over conservation spending Concerns are also being raised over the amount spent on conservation compared with the monument’s earnings. Not only the Royal Gate, but several other sections of the Taj Mahal complex have also deteriorated over time. Stones continue to break and fall from various parts of the monument. Despite the monument generating hundreds of crores in revenue, ASI data shows that approximately Rs 5 crore was spent on conservation work at the Taj Mahal during the last financial year. Kalander Bind said that conservation work is being carried out regularly and that restoration projects worth around Rs 5 crore have been completed at the monument.

stories.title: Are police killings of child-crime suspects revealing a pattern?:UP witnesses three such shooting deaths in a month
stories.summary: On May 5 in Hardoi, a 7-year-old child was allegedly sexually assaulted and murdered, triggering outrage across Uttar Pradesh. Within 12 hours, police killed the accused, Mehnoor, in an encounter. The incident reflects a shifting pattern in UP Police action, where encounters are increasingly being used not only against mafia and crimes against women, but also against those accused of crimes against children. Know what kind of crimes the police were strict about earlier What is the latest pattern? Taking action on crimes against children within hours 4 recent major incidents show that the police are taking very aggressive action against those who commit crimes against children. How the Yogi government worked in 9 years Focus on organised crime After Yogi Adityanath became Chief Minister in 2017, curbing organised crime became a major focus. In the first 10 months of his government, UP Police carried out 1,142 encounters in which 34 criminals were killed. The first encounter was of Gurmeet in Saharanpur on March 31, 2017. Later, police killed Naushad and Sarwar in Shamli on July 29. Naushad had 19 serious criminal cases against him, while Sarwar had 8. Ikram was killed in an encounter on August 10, followed by Nadeem on September 8 and Shamshad on September 10. Cracked down on crimes against women 'Operation Langda' launched Police adopted a strategy of psychological pressure for those who molested or committed violence against women and daughters. Videos were released showing the accused with bandages on their legs (limping) and apologizing. This sent a message that those who molest or rape women will not be spared. 2019-21: Taught lessons to those who attacked the uniform Encounter for murder or assault of police 2024: Action on those who commit major robberies 25 encounters in one year 2025: Contract killers killed 48 encounters in 2025 This year, a maximum of 48 criminals were killed in encounters. Especially, contract killers were the target of UP Police. Among them, Banarasi Yadav of Varanasi was the main one. 24 cases were registered against him. More than half of these were for contract killings. UPSTF killed him in Chaubepur. Similarly, STF encountered Mohammad Rehan of Shamli, accused in 90 cases. Ashu alias Monty of Moradabad was considered a sharpshooter. STF and Moradabad Police killed him in an encounter. Read what Retired IPS Lalji Shukla says Question: When and how does the police pattern against crime change? Retired IPS: Police strategy changes with changing crime patterns. Around 20 years ago, organized crime and highway robberies were common. Later, criminals began looting families at gunpoint inside homes and even firing at police during encounters. Crimes against women and children are highly emotional issues, and public anger rises sharply in such cases. With CCTV cameras now common, incidents are often captured on video, increasing pressure on police to act quickly. As crime patterns evolve, police response also changes accordingly. Question: How can this model benefit the UP elections? Retired IPS: People want to feel safe and usually support governments that provide security. With elections approaching, the Yogi government will likely try to further strengthen this law-and-order image. The impact of UP model on the Bengal elections After BJP's victory in West Bengal, the 'UP Police Model' is in the headlines. PM Modi, Home Minister Amit Shah, and CM Yogi explained to the public during the campaign how the mafia rule was ended in UP. How were state borders secured? On this, Mamata Banerjee had to say that Bengal does not need any 'external model'. The agenda of Maa-Maati-Manush (Mother, Soil, People) is fine.
